Native macOS observation of pnpm with an abandoned selector lock owner.
The cloned-home baseline succeeds, but dead-owner recovery times out.

The failing test clones the existing package-manager-store under its temporary
PNPM_HOME, removes only the clone's tmp state, and runs the same sandboxed argv:
/opt/homebrew/bin/pnpm exec /usr/bin/true
The cloned-home baseline passed within the unchanged 10-second child limit.
The test spawned /usr/bin/true, waited for it to exit, and verified signal-zero
returned ESRCH for PID 20012 before seeding the task-owned selector owner file.
No operator selector lock was modified. The clone was removed on test exit.

Captured assertion:
real pnpm must recover dead owner 20012-1009843231000000000-0 within the unchanged 10s child limit: Err(Timeout { timeout: 10s }); elapsed=10.500000000s; remaining_owner=Ok("20012-1009843231000000000-0")

This proves no autonomous recovery within the required limit for this fresh
abandoned-owner fixture under the current whole-home grant. It does not prove
pnpm never expires old locks, or identify why it retained this owner. No retry,
manual cleanup, longer deadline, or product recovery mechanism was added.
